kindHint.lvm-thin: Create the volume group and thin pool on each node first. Volumes are raw thin volumes kept on the node that creates them, and their snapshots hold disks only. Needs Linux nodes running as root.
kindHint.zfs: Create the dataset on each node first. Volumes are raw zvols kept on the node that creates them, and their snapshots hold disks only. Disks can only revert to their latest snapshot. Needs Linux nodes running as root.
kindHint.rbd: Create the Ceph pool first and put ceph.conf and the keyring on each node. Volumes are raw RBD images that every node of the pool can use, and their snapshots hold disks only. Needs Linux nodes with QEMU's rbd driver (qemu-block-extra) and the rbd command (ceph-common).
kindHint.lvm-shared: Create the shared volume group (vgcreate --shared) on a LUN every node sees first, and run lvmlockd with sanlock or dlm on each node. Volumes are raw logical volumes that every node of the pool can use, without snapshots. Needs Linux nodes running as root.

vmForm.maxMemoryHint: Leave empty for none. While running, memory can grow up to this on Linux nodes with virtio-mem. Takes effect from the next start.
vmForm.liveHint: vCPU cores and memory within the maximums apply right away where the node supports it. Other CPU, memory, firmware and machine changes apply at the next restart.
vmForm.runningNoteLive: The VM is running and its node cannot change. Hardware changes are applied while it runs where possible; the rest are listed on its page and apply at the next restart.
vmForm.restartForHotplug: The VM was started without hotplug support. Restart it once to add or remove disks and interfaces while it runs.
vmForm.disksLive: While the VM runs, volumes can be attached at the end (virtio-blk only, 8 devices at most) and disks attached while it runs can be removed from the end. Disks it started with cannot change.

vmForm.bootOrderRunning: Stop the VM to change the boot order.
vmForm.ciNote: Orbivisor attaches a NoCloud seed drive (label cidata). Cloud images and cloudbase-init read it at first boot.
vmForm.ciRunning: Changes apply at the next start of the VM (restart). A reboot inside the guest still sees the old settings.
vmForm.ciHostnameHint: Empty uses the VM name ({{name}}). A FQDN also sets the domain.
vmForm.ciUserHint: Renames the distribution's default user. Empty keeps its name.
vmForm.ciPasswordHint: Stored only as a SHA-512 crypt hash. A crypt hash ($6$…) is kept as it is. Empty means no password; SSH keys are safer.
vmForm.ciKeysHint: One key per line (ssh-ed25519, ssh-rsa, ecdsa-sha2-…).
vmForm.ciUserDataHint: Used as it is instead of the generated user-data (start with #cloud-config).
vmForm.ciVendorDataHint: Runs together with the generated user-data, for packages and runcmd.

haChecks.pageHint: Every node checks these links, ping targets and storage pool paths every 5 seconds and sends the results with its lease. placement.pageHint: Every node sends a load summary (CPU over 1 and 5 minutes, memory) with its lease every 5 seconds. Starting VMs, HA recovery and node draining choose the node with the best score. Every 5 minutes the balancer looks at how uneven the nodes are and recommends, or makes, live migrations.

modeHint.recommend: The balancer only recommends moves; apply them yourself.
modeHint.auto: The balancer starts up to two live migrations at a time by itself.

policyHint.pack: Fill busy nodes first, keeping others free. The balancer only fixes broken hard rules.

placement.thresholdHint: From 1 to 50 percent. The balancer starts moving VMs when the imbalance (the mean of the CPU and memory spread across nodes) is above this and goes on until it is below 0.8 times this. A node whose CPU or memory use is more than twice this above the average is relieved even when the imbalance is lower.

pausedReasons.pack: The policy is pack, so the balancer does not move VMs for balance.

errors.gateway: Use an address of the subnet's family.
errors.dns: Give at most 4 IP addresses, separated by commas.
errors.pools: Use ranges like 10.10.0.100-10.10.0.199 (at most 16), in the subnet's family.

subnets.title: Subnets
subnets.none: No subnets: interfaces get no addresses.
subnets.gatewayHint: Optional. Defaults to the first host address; always reserved.
subnets.poolsHint: Optional. Defaults to the whole subnet.
subnets.noDhcp6: IPv6: no DHCP switch here; choose an IPv6 mode for RA or DHCPv6.
subnets.editHint: The CIDR and gateway of a saved subnet cannot change (remove it and add it again). A subnet can be removed only when no interface uses its addresses. When you add a subnet, interfaces that have no address get one from it (running guests pick it up at their next DHCP renewal); interfaces that already have an address keep it (fill a missing family with orbivisorctl network ips NAME --fill).
subnets.fillNotice_one: 1 interface on this network has no address; saving gives it one from the new subnet. Its port is off until then.
subnets.fillNotice_other: {{count}} interfaces on this network have no address; saving gives each one from the new subnet. Their ports are off until then.
subnets.conflict: Someone changed the subnets meanwhile (now: {{subnets}}). Your rows are kept; check them and save again.
subnets.floatingHint: Optional. Router outside addresses and floating IPs come from here; without it they share the allocation ranges.
subnets.ipv6ModeHint: Router advertisements go out only when the network is a router interface. SLAAC modes need a /64 and give EUI-64 addresses.

sheet.title: Network {{name}}
sheet.detachDescription: The router's port on this network goes away: guests lose the default route at their next DHCP renewal. Floating IPs and load balancer VIPs that use this path must be removed first.

ips.title: IP addresses
ips.liveError: Could not read the port state from OVN: {{error}}
ips.hidden_one: 1 more interface belongs to a VM you cannot see; it counts in the usage above.
ips.hidden_other: {{count}} more interfaces belong to VMs you cannot see; they count in the usage above.
ips.offHint: Its port passes nothing until it gets an address: type one in Edit (the VM may keep running), or run orbivisorctl network ips NAME --fill.

sdn.noChassis: No node is a ready OVN chassis
sdn.notReadyHint: SDN networks need SDN (OVN) set up first, under Networks › SDN.
sdn.statusUnknown: Cannot read the SDN state ({{error}}); the server checks it when you create the network.
sdn.mtuHint: 1280–9000. Defaults to 1442: a 1500-byte underlay minus the 58-byte Geneve header.

wizard.title: Set up SDN (OVN)
wizard.centralsHint: Central nodes run the OVN NB and SB databases (Raft) and northd. Choose 1, 3 or 5; the first is set up first and the others join it one at a time. Three voting members are chosen for you. Packages are installed with apt.
wizard.address: Central address of the first node (optional)
wizard.addressHint: The address the databases listen on. Defaults to the node's address; it must be the node's address or one of its cluster link addresses (not loopback or link-local).
wizard.chassisHint: Every node that runs VMs on SDN networks must be a ready chassis. Central nodes already are. New nodes that join later are not installed by themselves.

centrals.title: Central nodes
centrals.hint: A fixed set you choose (1, 3 or 5). Changing it copies the databases; one change runs at a time.
centrals.removeDescription: An online node leaves the NB and SB databases and stops them; its database files are renamed, not deleted, and it stays a chassis. An offline node is kicked out of the databases by another central instead (its own files are left as they are).
centrals.addDescription: Installs the OVN central packages on the node with apt and joins it to the NB and SB databases.

sdn.noNodes: No other node can become a central.

move.hint: The setup stopped on {{node}}, which is offline or gone, before any central was up. Move the setup to another node.

sdn.serverChecks: The server checks that SDN (OVN) is set up when you create the network.

strays.title: Leftover central databases
strays.hint: These nodes may still be members of the OVN database cluster although they are not central nodes, which narrows its failure margin. Remove them.
strays.held: {{name}} holds OVN central databases but is not a central.
strays.gone: {{name}} was removed from the cluster but may still be an OVN database member.
strays.removeNamed: Remove the leftover central databases of {{name}}
strays.removeTitle: Remove the leftover OVN central databases of {{name}}?
strays.removeDescription: An online node leaves the databases and stops them (its files are renamed, not deleted). An offline or removed node is kicked out by a live central.

physnet.title: SDN physical networks
physnet.editDescription: Link physical networks (physnets) to Linux bridges you made on this node, and make the node a gateway candidate for routers.
physnet.name: Physical network
physnet.bridgeHint: The bridge must exist on the node. The SDN agent links it to OVS with a veth pair and does not change the bridge.
physnet.priorityHint: 1–1000. Higher goes first; routers spread across candidates with the same priority.
physnet.gatewayPending: (the SDN agent has not applied it yet)
physnet.pickHint: The name nodes link to a bridge under Nodes › node › SDN physical networks.
physnet.noneHint: No node has a physical network yet. Add one on a node's page first (Nodes › node › SDN physical networks).
physnet.vlanHint: Optional, 1–4094. Without it the network is flat (untagged).

errors.name: Use a lowercase letter, then up to 30 lowercase letters, digits or -.
errors.duplicate: This physical network is listed twice.
errors.bridge: Use the name of a Linux bridge (1–15 characters, not br-int).

lockdown.title: OVN access lockdown
lockdown.hint: Chassis can only change their own rows in the southbound database, only northd writes through the privileged port, and the OVN ports accept only the addresses of cluster members. A node removed from the cluster is cut off even though its certificate is still valid.
lockdown.turningOn: Turn on the OVN access lockdown
lockdown.turningOff: Turn off the OVN access lockdown
lockdown.checkSets: {{members}} member addresses and {{centrals}} central addresses will be allowed.
lockdown.noOutside: Nothing outside the allow list is connected to a central now.
lockdown.outside_one: {{count}} connection to a central comes from outside the allow list. It is cut off when the lockdown turns on (a member node behind NAT or a removed node).
lockdown.outside_other: {{count}} connections to centrals come from outside the allow list. They are cut off when the lockdown turns on (member nodes behind NAT or removed nodes).
lockdown.force: Turn on anyway (these connections are cut off)
lockdown.offTitle: Turn off the OVN access lockdown?
lockdown.offDescription: The allow lists come down first, then each central goes back to the plain ports. Any node with the cluster certificate can then write to the southbound database again.

alerts.title: SDN alerts
alerts.dialogDescription: Creates the recommended SDN rules (quorum, centrals, chassis, gateways, sync, physical networks, load balancer members). They are ordinary rules afterwards. Rules that already exist are skipped.
alerts.created_one: Created {{count}} SDN alert rule; {{existing}} already existed.
alerts.created_other: Created {{count}} SDN alert rules; {{existing}} already existed.

router.pageHint: Routers connect SDN networks to each other and, through an external (provider) network, to the outside with SNAT and floating IPs.
router.sdnNotReady: Routers and floating IPs need SDN (OVN) set up first, under Networks › SDN.

empty.title: No routers
empty.description: Create a router to connect SDN networks and reach the outside.

router.createDescription: Pick the SDN networks to connect and, optionally, an external network for the way out.
router.deleteDescription: The router has no interfaces left. Its outside addresses go back to the external network.
router.externalHint: A provider network. Without one, the router only connects its SDN networks to each other.
router.externalChangeHint: Keeping the same network keeps the outside addresses. Floating IPs routed through this router must be detached before you change or clear it.
router.noExternalHint: No external network: the router only connects its SDN networks.
router.snatLabel: Translate inside IPv4 addresses to the outside address (SNAT)
router.snatOffHint: Without SNAT the physical router needs routes to the inside subnets via the router's outside address.
router.interfacesHint: An SDN network can be an interface of one router. Its subnet gateways become the router's addresses; guests get the default route at their next DHCP renewal.
router.noAttachable: No SDN network with subnets is free to connect.
router.noRoutesDefault: No static routes. The default route goes to the external network's gateway.
router.firstGatewayHint: Top-ranked. The active one is in the router.
router.gatewaysHint: OVN moves the router's outside port to the next node when the active one fails (BFD). Open SNAT connections are cut then.
router.gatewayError: No gateway node has the physical network of {{network}} ready. The router's outside port stays off (no SNAT or floating IPs) until one has: set it under Nodes › node › SDN physical networks.
router.liveError: Could not read the active gateway from OVN: {{error}}
router.upstreamHint: These routes are not translated. The physical router needs them:

errors.nexthop: Use an address of the same family as the destination.
errors.defaultRoute: With an external network the default route is set automatically.

router.activeUnknown: Unknown: OVN could not be read
router.gatewayErrorAsk: No gateway node has the physical network of {{network}} ready, so the router's outside port stays off (no SNAT or floating IPs). Ask an administrator to give a gateway node that physical network.

fip.pageHint: Public addresses from an external network, mapped one to one to a VM interface. They are distributed (leave from the VM's node) when that node has the physical network, otherwise the gateway node handles them.

empty.title: No floating IPs
empty.description: Create a floating IP from an external network and attach it to a routed VM interface.

fip.createDescription: Takes a free address from the external network's floating IP ranges.
fip.deleteDescription: The address goes back to the external network.
fip.deleteAttached: It is attached: its NAT goes away and the address goes back to the external network.
fip.attachDescription: Interfaces on SDN networks routed to {{network}} can take it.
fip.detachDescription: The VM keeps its private address; connections through the floating IP stop.
fip.addressHint: Leave empty to take the next free one.
fip.nameHint: Defaults to the address with dashes (203-0-113-120).
fip.noProvider: No external network you can use
fip.nicHint: Only interfaces on a network that is an interface of a router with this external network, and that have an IPv4 address.
fip.noRoutableNic: No interface is routed to this external network yet: connect its network to a router whose external network is this one.

server.someNodeNoPhysnet: A node of the VM does not have physical network {{physnet}} ready

lb.pageHint: A load balancer spreads one virtual address (VIP) on an SDN network over VM interfaces or addresses (TCP·UDP). Health checks take dead members out; an external VIP opens it to the physical network.
lb.sdnNotReady: Load balancers need SDN (OVN) set up first, under Networks › SDN.

empty.title: No load balancers
empty.description: Create a load balancer on an SDN network that is attached to a router.

lb.createDescription: The VIP and the health check addresses come from the subnet pools.
lb.deleteDescription: Its VIP, external VIP and health check addresses go back to their networks. Open connections through the VIP stop.
lb.liveError: Couldn't read the health checks from OVN: {{error}}
lb.healthCheck: Health check every {{interval}} s, timeout {{timeout}} s, up after {{rise}}, down after {{fall}}
lb.noHealthCheck: No health check: every member is always used.
lb.vipNetworkHint: An SDN network with an IPv4 subnet that is an interface of a router.
lb.noVipNetwork: No SDN network attached to a router
lb.vipHint: Empty: the next free address of the subnet pool.
lb.externalOn: External VIP on {{network}} (the router's external network)
lb.externalNone: External VIP (the router of this network has no external network)
lb.externalIpHint: Empty: the next free floating IP. It counts toward the folder's floating IP quota.
lb.affinityHint: The same client goes to the same member for this long (1 to 65535).
lb.noUsableNic: No VM interface on this router's networks can be a member.

errors.memberTaken: This member is already in the listener.

topology.big: This is a large picture. Pick a network folder or hide VMs to make it easier to read.

migration.title: Migrate {{name}} to SDN
migration.description: Moves the VM interfaces of this simple network to an SDN network, keeping their addresses. Each VM moves stopped, live (about a second without network) or with a restart; a temporary bridge connects both sides until you finish.
migration.createNew: A new SDN network with the same subnet
migration.cidrHint: The subnet of the source network, so the addresses stay.
migration.gatewayHint: The physical router's address: it stays the default route while the bridge is up.

modeHint.auto: Stopped VMs change in place; running VMs move live when they can, otherwise they restart.
modeHint.live: Running VMs move live (tap moved, about a second without network). VMs that can't are blocked.
modeHint.restart: Running VMs are shut down, changed and started again.
modeHint.offline: Only stopped VMs move. Running VMs are blocked.

migration.allowShrink: Move live even if the guest's MTU shrinks
migration.bridgeHint: Moved and remaining VMs stay on one L2 through a bridge (OVN l2gateway) on one node until you finish.
migration.bridgeNodeAuto: Automatic (the node with the most VMs)
migration.planHint: Nothing has changed yet. Fix an address, leave a VM out or change the mode, then plan again. Blocked VMs are skipped.
migration.instanceIdBanner: Some VMs use cloud-init: their instance-id changes, so on the next boot the guest runs its per-instance setup again (for example new SSH host keys).
migration.noNics: No VM has an interface on this network.
migration.newBridgeNodeHint: The bridge node was removed from the cluster. Pick another node to resume.
migration.rollbackDescription: The VMs go back to the source network with their security groups and cloud-init addresses; running VMs move live (or restart if the MTU would shrink). The bridge comes down when the last VM is back.
migration.finishHint: Finishing removes the bridge. You can attach {{target}} to a router at the same time so the router becomes the default gateway.
migration.finishLeft_one: {{count}} interface is still on the source network.
migration.finishLeft_other: {{count}} interfaces are still on the source network.
migration.routerHint: The router port takes the subnet gateway address: DHCP guests switch at the next renewal, static guests right away.
migration.deleteDescription: The migration stops where it is and its bridge comes down. Moved VMs stay on the SDN network.
migration.deleteRecordDescription: Only the record goes away. The VMs stay as they are.

text.busy: the VM is in another migration
text.onTarget: another interface of the VM is already on {{network}}
text.noMac: the interface has no MAC address yet
text.reserved: {{ip}} is reserved in {{network}} (network, broadcast or gateway)
text.duplicate: {{ip}} is also planned for another interface
text.notChassis: the VM runs on a node without OVN: move it to an SDN node or stop it first
text.runningOffline: the VM is running (mode: stopped VMs only)
text.liveChassis: can't move live: the VM's node has no OVN
text.liveMtu: can't move live: the guest's MTU would shrink
text.liveAddress: can't move live: the address is not known
text.ipam: the address changes: a new one comes from the target's pool
text.noAgent: no guest agent: the guest's current address is not known
text.mtu: the MTU shrinks from {{from}} to {{to}} (DHCP guests get the new MTU)
text.instanceId: the cloud-init instance-id changes: on the next boot the guest runs its per-instance setup again (for example new SSH host keys)
text.noGroups: the interface has no security groups: traffic is not filtered on SDN either
text.restartGap: the VM is shut down and started again
text.providerNoBridge: the target is a physical network: no bridge, so moved and remaining VMs reach each other only on the same L2
text.noBridge: no bridge: moved VMs can't reach the VMs still on the source
text.dhcp: a DHCP server on the source network also answers moved VMs over the bridge: reserve the same addresses there or turn it off while migrating
text.bridgeOverlay: a bridge only goes to an SDN overlay network
text.badBridgeNode: node {{node}} can't be the bridge node (no OVN or no source bridge)
text.noBridgeNode: no OVN node has the source bridge {{bridge}}
text.bridgeRemoved: the bridge node {{node}} was removed from the cluster: resume with another bridge node
text.ipamOthers: IPAM does not know the addresses other hosts use on the source network: keep them out of the target's pools while the bridge is up

migration.oneMode: One mode for the whole migration — leave VMs out and migrate them in a second migration for a different mode.
migration.hiddenVms_one: {{count}} VM you cannot see is on the source network; it is not moved.
migration.hiddenVms_other: {{count}} VMs you cannot see are on the source network; they are not moved.
migration.replanFirst: You changed the mode or an address: plan again before starting.
migration.changedDescription: The server planned again when it created the migration, and some interfaces now differ from the plan on screen. Check them before starting. If you don't start, the migration stays planned: you can start or delete it in the next step.
migration.changedDisrupts_one: {{count}} running VM would now lose its network briefly or be restarted.
migration.changedDisrupts_other: {{count}} running VMs would now lose their network briefly or be restarted.
